Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  Acute sudden-onset left-sided headache beginning ~4 hours prior to consult; visual disturbance (blurred vision with zigzag lines), dizziness; nausea with two episodes of vomiting at onset; screen intolerance. First episode of this type. Past history: kidney stones.  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Mother with migraines; family history of hypothyroidism.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  Paracetamol (acetaminophen) taken once today; dose/route/frequency not documented. No regular medications reported. No known drug allergies.  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  Pregnancy considered unlikely by patient. Otherwise not recorded.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  Not recorded.  
- Hearing and vision concerns:  Vision blurred with zigzag lines; cannot tolerate screens. Hearing concerns not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key clinical findings: First episode of acute left-sided headache with visual aura (blurred vision with zigzag lines), nausea/vomiting (x2 at onset), dizziness, photophobia/screen intolerance; no reported limb weakness or gait disturbance by history. Paracetamol provided no relief. Family history of migraine (mother).  
- Reasoning and impression: Presentation is most consistent with migraine with visual aura. Sudden onset and first-ever severe headache with vomiting are red flags warranting in-person assessment to exclude secondary causes.  
- Working diagnosis: Migraine with visual aura. Supported by unilateral head pain, visual aura phenomena, nausea/vomiting, photophobia, and positive family history (consistent with DDx).  
- Considerations (from DDx, consistent with transcript):  
  - Subarachnoid hemorrhage (aneurysmal SAH): medium concern given first sudden-onset headache with vomiting; absence of exam/vitals leaves uncertainty.  
  - Cervical artery dissection: low likelihood but considered due to unilateral acute headache and dizziness; no trauma or focal deficits reported.  
  - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST): low likelihood; presentation favors migraine, risk factors not elicited.  
- Management/plan (per transcript):  
  - Trial ibuprofen; dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  - Add anti-sickness medication available from pharmacy; specific agent and dose not documented.  
  - Hydration including sugary carbonated drink (e.g., cola).  
  - Same-day in-person appointment planned for full neurological examination; patient advised to cancel if symptoms resolve after treatment.  
  - Safety-net: Contact clinic for any worsening or new neurological symptoms; seek urgent care if severe or not improving.  
- Conflict noted: None between transcript and DDx.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Education provided that migraines can present at various ages; overview of stepped treatment (NSAID + antiemetic; potential escalation if needed). Red flag advice given (seek care if not improving or worsening).

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Migraine with visual aura — Likelihood: High. Justified by unilateral headache, visual zigzag aura, photophobia/screen intolerance, nausea/vomiting, and family history; no focal deficits reported.  
- Subarachnoid hemorrhage — Likelihood: Medium. First sudden-onset headache with vomiting at onset is a red flag; lack of examination/vitals maintains uncertainty.  
- Cervical artery dissection — Likelihood: Low. Unilateral acute headache with dizziness; no neck pain/trauma or focal neurological signs reported.

Quality checks

- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vitals (including BP), full neurological and eye examination, BMI/anthropometry, urinalysis, immunization review (influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus), chronic disease risk assessment (CVD, diabetes), lifestyle risk factors (tobacco/alcohol/physical activity/diet), cancer screenings (cervical, breast, bowel), osteoporosis risk/DEXA where indicated, mood screening.  
- Internal conflicts or contradictions between transcript and DDx: None material. Note: Sudden onset and ongoing visual symptoms are atypical for classic aura and warrant in-person assessment as planned.  
- Transcript quality notes: Telehealth consult with brief connection issue; no physical examination performed; some history elements not elicited.
